newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil not expected to comment on coffee quota cut.
newsitem.headline: Brazil not expected to comment on coffee quota cut.

text.p: Brazilian officials are not expected to comment on a proposed cut in coffee exports in the first half 1997 in a meeting today with African coffee leaders, an Ivorian embassy official said.
Rather, at most Brazilian representatives will express their support for an emergency meeting of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC), he added.
"The best the Brazilian authorities can do is to say that they support the call for an emergency ACPC meeting," the embassy official said.

The head of Brazil's primary commodities department at the Industry and Commerce ministry Mauricio Assis and officials from the Foreign Affairs ministry are currently meeting with a delegation led by Ivorian Commodities Minister Guy-Alain Gauze.
The delegation earlier this week reached agreement with Colombian coffee officials that exports by ACPC members needed to be cut by around 2.5 million bags in first half 1997.
Already there is speculation ACPC countries may meet in mid-January. One possible venue is Brazil where an international seminar is due to be held on January 20-22 in Rio de Janeiro.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
